title: Equivariant splitting of weight-two additive central extensions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$, with multiplication, inverse and identity obeying the group identities; it is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On $S$-schemes use the fppf topology, whose covering families are jointly surjective flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. Write $\mathbf G_a(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ with addition and $\mathbf G_m(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$ with multiplication, for every $S$-scheme $T$. A group sheaf means a group-valued functor with unique gluing of compatible sections for these coverings. A central exact sequence means that its first map identifies its source with the kernel of its second map, the second map is locally surjective for this topology, and the kernel commutes with every local section of the middle sheaf. Let $Z$ be a separated commutative $S$-group scheme, and let $1\to Z\xrightarrow{i}F\xrightarrow{q}\mathbf G_a\to0$ be a central exact sequence of group sheaves. Suppose $\mathbf G_m$ acts on $F$ by group-sheaf automorphisms, fixes $i(Z)$ pointwise, and induces multiplication by $t^k$ on the quotient $\mathbf G_a$, for a fixed $k\in\{2,-2\}$. Then $F$ is commutative and $q$ admits a unique $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant group-sheaf section $j:\mathbf G_a\to F$. In addition, every group-sheaf homomorphism $f:\mathbf G_a\to Z$ satisfying $f(t^k u)=f(u)$ for all local units $t$ and sections $u$ is the trivial homomorphism.

proof.text: For local sections $u,v$ of $\mathbf G_a$, choose fppf-local lifts $x,y$ in $F$. The commutator $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ has quotient zero, hence equals $i(c(u,v))$ for a unique local section of $Z$. Replacing $x,y$ by $i(z)x,i(w)y$ leaves this expression unchanged since $i(Z)$ is central. Therefore these local sections agree on overlaps and glue uniquely in the sheaf $Z$; they are natural under every base change. This defines $c:\mathbf G_a\times\mathbf G_a\to Z$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.127, additive commutator paragraph, and Lemma 4.3.2, printed p.128; explicit sheaf and fppf-cover details.

proof.text: Every commutator in $F$ belongs to the central subgroup $i(Z)$. Consequently $[xx\prime,y]=[x,y][x\prime,y]$ and $[x,yy\prime]=[x,y][x,y\prime]$: expand the products and move the central commutators past the other factors. Applying these identities to lifts of $u,u\prime,v,v\prime$ proves that $c$ is additive in each argument (written multiplicatively in $Z$). Moreover $\alpha_t([x,y])=[\alpha_t(x),\alpha_t(y)]$, while $\alpha_t$ fixes $i(Z)$; hence $c(t^ku,t^kv)=c(u,v)$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.127, additive commutator paragraph, and Lemma 4.3.2, printed p.128; explicit sheaf and fppf-cover details.

proof.text: For any local unit $a$, [lem-sfb-unit-power-fppf-surjective] with $n=2$ gives, after an fppf cover, a unit $t$ with $t^k=a$: take a square root of $a$ if $k=2$, and of $a^{-1}$ if $k=-2$. The equality in step 2 then gives $c(au,av)=c(u,v)$ locally, hence globally by sheaf separation. Replacing $v$ by $a^{-1}v$ gives $c(au,v)=c(u,a^{-1}v)$ for every unit $a$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.127, additive commutator paragraph, and Lemma 4.3.2, printed p.128; explicit sheaf and fppf-cover details.

proof.text: Work over an affine test scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-sfb-monic-principal-open-fppf], the algebra $A[t,1/(t(t+1)(t^2+t+1))]$ supplies an fppf cover on which $t,t+1$ and $\delta=(t+1)^{-1}-t^{-1}-1=-(t^2+t+1)/(t(t+1))$ are units. Biadditivity and step 3 give $c(u,\delta v)=c(u,(t+1)^{-1}v)c(u,t^{-1}v)^{-1}c(u,v)^{-1}=c((t+1)u,v)c(tu,v)^{-1}c(u,v)^{-1}=1$. Replace $v$ by $\delta^{-1}v$. Thus $c(u,v)=1$ on this cover and hence on the test scheme. Affine opens cover every test scheme, so $c=1$ everywhere. The definition in step 1 shows that every pair of sections of $F$ commutes; thus $F$ is commutative.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.127, additive commutator paragraph, and Lemma 4.3.2, printed p.128; explicit sheaf and fppf-cover details.

proof.text: Let $f:\mathbf G_a\to Z$ satisfy the stated invariance. On each affine test scheme choose, by [lem-sfb-monic-principal-open-fppf] for $P(t)=t(t^2-1)$, an fppf-local unit $t$ with $t^2-1$ invertible. For either sign of $k$, $a=t^k-1$ is a unit: for $k=-2$ it equals $-(t^2-1)t^{-2}$. Since $f$ is a homomorphism, $f(au)=f(t^ku)f(u)^{-1}=1$. Replace $u$ by $a^{-1}u$ and descend equality in the sheaf $Z$. This proves the final assertion of the item, over every base change.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.127, additive commutator paragraph, and Lemma 4.3.2, printed p.128; explicit sheaf and fppf-cover details.

proof.text: Write the now commutative $F$ additively. Work on an affine open of $S$ and then on the fppf cover from [lem-sfb-monic-principal-open-fppf] with $P(t)=t(t^2-1)$; put $a=t^k-1$, a unit. For $u\in\mathbf G_a(T)$ choose local lifts $x$ of $u$ and set $d(u)=\alpha_t(x)-x$. A different lift is $x+i(z)$, and $\alpha_t$ fixes $i(z)$, so the difference is unchanged. It glues uniquely in $F$, naturally in $T$. Lifting $u,v$ by $x,y$ and $u+v$ by $x+y$ proves $d(u+v)=d(u)+d(v)$. Also $q(d(u))=au$. Define $j(u)=d(a^{-1}u)$; this is a homomorphism and $qj=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.127, additive commutator paragraph, and Lemma 4.3.2, printed p.128; explicit sheaf and fppf-cover details.

proof.text: For a local unit $s$ and a lift $x$ of $u$, the section $\alpha_s(x)$ lifts $s^ku$. Since the actions of $s$ and $t$ commute, $d(s^ku)=\alpha_t\alpha_s(x)-\alpha_s(x)=\alpha_s(d(u))$. Multiplication by the scalar $a^{-1}$ commutes with multiplication by $s^k$ on $\mathbf G_a$, so $j(s^ku)=\alpha_s(j(u))$. Thus every local section just constructed is $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, printed p.127, additive commutator paragraph, and Lemma 4.3.2, printed p.128; explicit sheaf and fppf-cover details.

proof.text: If $j_1,j_2$ are two equivariant homomorphic sections over any base change, their difference takes values in $i(Z)$ because $qj_1=qj_2$. Since $F$ is commutative, it defines a homomorphism $f:\mathbf G_a\to Z$; equivariance and the trivial action on $Z$ imply $f(t^ku)=f(u)$. Step 5 gives $f=0$, hence $j_1=j_2$. Apply this uniqueness on overlaps of the affine and fppf base covers used in step 6. For every test scheme, pull back these covers and glue the resulting values of $j(u)$ using the sheaf property of $F$. Uniqueness makes the glued values natural in the test scheme; the homomorphism, section and equivariance identities hold locally and thus globally. This gives the required unique global equivariant group-sheaf section.

Step 3: fppf square roots, with t^2 = a^-1 for k = -2, give c(au,v) = c(u,a^-1 v). Step 7: equivariance follows because the actions commute. Step 8: uniqueness from step 5, then descent along the fppf cover and gluing over affine opens.
